answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because canyon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, shale is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any tundra approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
